thresholds: SEV1 if error rate > 10% or sustained > 30 min; SEV2 if 5-10%; SEV3 if < 5%.
body: Checkout depends on payments-client. A circuit breaker OPEN means payments is failing and checkout is shedding load. If error rate is 5-10% and the breaker has tripped, declare SEV2, page the payments on-call, and post in #incidents. Cached-cart fallback keeps browsing alive, so customer impact is partial.

thresholds: SEV1 if processor success rate < 90%; SEV2 if 90-97%; SEV3 otherwise.
body: 402 spikes usually indicate a processor-side issue. Check the processor status page, fail over to the backup processor if success rate < 95%, and notify finance if charges may be affected.

thresholds: SEV3 for latency-only alerts that auto-resolve.
body: Slow index warm-up after a deploy is expected and self-heals. No action unless p99 stays above 1000ms for over 15 minutes.
